{{Quote|General Kenobi. You are the first Jedi I have entertained at our education center. Few possess a Jedi's resolve, and it is strength of will that is my greatest enemy.|Keeper Agruss|<ref name="Slaves" />}}
'''Agruss''', also known as the "'''Keeper'''," was the head of the [[Kadavo slave processing facility/Legends|Kadavo slave processing facility]] on [[Kadavo/Legends|Kadavo]] at the time that [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] was imprisoned there. He was a cruel [[Slaver/Legends|slaver]] who did not hesitate to end the lives of several [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved beings]] in an attempt to break the morale of his captive [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]].

When [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] led Republic forces on a rescue mission, Agruss tried to dispose of the remaining slaves by dumping them in the caldera. Most of the [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] captives were saved by the Jedi at the last moment, and Agruss was impaled by [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] with an [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]].

==Biography==

===Early career===
{{Quote|Come now Master Kenobi, I know a Jedi won't kill an unarmed man!''"<br />"''I'm no Jedi.|Agruss just as he is killed by Captain Rex|<ref name="Escape" />}}
[[File:KadavoProcessingFacility-EscapefromKadavo.png|thumb|250x250px|The [[Kadavo slave processing facility/Legends|Kadavo slave processing facility]], Agruss' base of operation.]]
[[Keeper/Legends|Keeper]] Agruss was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slaver/Legends|slaver]] who served the [[Zygerrian Slave Empire/Legends|Zygerrian Slave Empire]], which worked with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. Using a [[Repulsorlift chair/Legends|hover chair]]<ref name="Slaves" /> and exuding an air of decadence,<ref name="SWE" /> he oversaw the [[Kadavo slave processing facility/Legends|Kadavo slave processing facility]], the center of [[Slavery/Legends|slaving]] operations on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kadavo/Legends|Kadavo]].<ref name="Slaves" /> Ironically, a lifetime of excesses had left Agruss as physically weaker than the slaves, but his [[Repulsorlift chair/Legends|hover chair]] was lined with instruments that allowed him to punish those under his command.<ref>{{SWE|1=locations|2=kadavo|3=Kadavo}}</ref> 

===Final assigment on Kadavo===
[[File:AgrussWelcomesKenobi-SotR.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Agruss welcomes Kenobi to his "education center"|left]]
In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Slaves of the Republic Date">{{TCWdates|412}}</ref> the captured [[Togruta/Legends|Togruta]] population of the planet [[Kiros/Legends|Kiros]] was sent to Kadavo to undergo processing under Agruss's supervision. However, the disappearance of Kiros's residents had not escaped the notice of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and an investigation led three Jedi&mdash;[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], and [[Ahsoka Tano/Legends|Ahsoka Tano]]&mdash;and [[Clone Captain/Legends|Clone Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|CT-7567]], "Rex," to the [[Zygerria/Legends|Zygerrian homeworld]], where all were captured by Zygerrian forces.<ref name="Slaves" />

While Skywalker and Tano remained captive on Zygerria, Kenobi, Rex, and Kiros [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Roshti/Legends|Roshti]] were sent to the processing hub on Kadavo. Agruss was on hand to greet Kenobi when he and his fellow captives arrived on the planet,<ref name="Slaves" /> as he was the first ever [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] to be interred at his grueling facility.<ref name="SWE" /> While the Keeper expressed his excitement at having a Jedi at the processing facility, he immediately demonstrated his authority in an attempt to force Kenobi into submission&mdash;without warning, Agruss<ref name="Slaves" /> had cruelly<ref name=":0">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/slaves-of-the-republic-episode-guide|text="Slaves of the Republic" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref> several Togruta slaves dropped into the [[Volcano/Legends|volcano]] above which the processing hub rested. He proclaimed that any attempt at disobedience on Kenobi's part would only result in the further suffering of others.<ref name="Slaves" /> Even Kenobi's attempts at helping the Togruta slaves backfired, causing them to avoid the Jedi or risk further pain. To prevent any more needless deaths or suffering, Obi-Wan kept his head down,<ref name="Escape" /> laboring under Agruss' cruel glare in seeming obedience.<ref name="SWE" />
[[File:AgrussRexKenobi-EFK.jpg|thumb|250x250px|Agruss before he can execute [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Rex/Legends|Rex]].]]
Agruss, under the order of Count [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]], prepared to execute Obi-Wan and Rex, but the men of the Republic overpowered the guards while Anakin Skywalker and Ahsoka Tano led an assault by clone forces to liberate the slaves.<ref name="Escape" /> Desperate<ref name="SW-Escape from Kadavo Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/escape-from-kadavo-episode-guide|text="Escape from Kadavo" Episode Guide &#124; The Clone Wars}}</ref> under threat of capture or worse, Arguss tortured Togruta slaves to force the Republic troops to stop, then destroyed the control panels that would have enabled their rescue. At this moment, Obi-Wan took possession of his lightsaber and pointed it at the slavemaster, who scoffed and claimed that the moralistic Jedi would not kill an unarmed man. Rex, enraged by the treatment of his men, the slaves and the Jedi at the hands of Arguss,<ref name="Escape" /> had no such reservations.<ref name="SWE" /> He quipped that he was no Jedi and threw an electrostaff taken from a guard. Arguss was impaled by the weapon and, in distress and agony, he flew his repulsorchair into a bank of monitors and was electrocuted. His corpse was incinerated when the labor processing hub was destroyed by Republic forces after their personnel were evacuated.<ref name="Escape" />

==Personality and traits==
An overweigth [[Zygerrian/Legends|Zygerrian]] [[Slavery/Legends|slavemaster]]<ref name="Slaves" /> who led the slaving operation on Kadavo, Agruss delighted in his superiority over his pathetic charges. He flaunted his power freely, punishing and executing slaves at a whim to ensure no one every questioned his authority. Though Agruss exhibited zeal in lording over slaves, he was hardly the model Zygerrians.<ref name="Slaves" /> Most Zygerrians were more powerfully built and physically fit,<ref name="Slaves" /> while Agruss had let corruption shape him.<ref name="Slaves" /> Aside of his cruelty, he was also a coward as he attemted to plea for his life after his prisoners had rebelled.<ref name="Escape" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:KeeperZygerrian.jpg|thumb|left|150px|"Keeper," as he appeared in the ''Slaves of the Republic'' comic arc]]
The character who would later be named Agruss<ref name=":0" /> was originally created by [[Henry Gilroy]] for the first story arc of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (comic series)|''The Clone Wars'' comic series]], [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic|''Slaves of the Republic'']]. Identified only as "Keeper," he appeared as one of the Zygerrian antagonists in the [[The Clone Wars 5|fifth]] and [[The Clone Wars 6|sixth issues]] of the series, both of which were released in [[2009]].<ref name="The Clone Wars 5">[[The Clone Wars 5|''The Clone Wars'' 5]]</ref>

In late [[2011]] and early [[2012]], the ''Slaves of the Republic'' comics were adapted into a three-part story arc of [[The Clone Wars: Season Four|Season Four]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'' TV series]]. Because the three episodes&mdash;"[[Kidnapped]],"<ref name="Kidnapped">{{TCW|Kidnapped}}</ref> "[[Slaves of the Republic]],"<ref name="Slaves" /> and "[[Escape from Kadavo]]"<ref name="Escape" />&mdash;were not direct adaptations of the comic arc, many differences existed between the two versions of the story. While the basic plot remained the same, the Keeper and several other characters underwent significant transformations for their TV appearances. Voiced by [[Victor Brandt]], the Keeper appeared in "Slaves of the Republic" and "Escape from Kadavo,"<ref name="Slaves" /><ref name="Escape" /> first receiving the name Agruss in the former's online guide on [[StarWars.com]].<ref name="Escape" />

"Escape from Kadavo" introduced a continuity error involving Agruss's fate.<ref name="Escape" /> In the comic conclusion to the story arc, the Keeper is arrested for his slaving activities;<ref name="The Clone Wars 6">[[The Clone Wars 6|''The Clone Wars'' 6]]</ref> in the TV conclusion to the story he is killed by Captain Rex.<ref name="Escape" /> As ''The Clone Wars'' TV series constitutes a higher form of [[canon]] than the comic series, the events of the TV series take precedence, indicating that death is Agruss's canonical fate.
